title: The best Housecall Pro alternatives for small teams in 2026
summary: Compare nine Housecall Pro alternatives for small home-service businesses, including pricing, best-fit use cases, drawbacks, and options for websites, SEO, scheduling, and more.
body_markdown:
Housecall Pro covers much of the day-to-day work of running a home-service business. However, cost often drives business owners to look for alternatives. Other times, a growing business needs more marketing tools than Housecall Pro offers.


The tools in this article take different approaches to managing the office work that keeps a home service business humming. Some focus on scheduling, dispatch, and invoicing. Others lean into mobile workflows, while a few put more emphasis on websites, local SEO, and marketing.


Here are eight Housecall Pro alternatives worth considering, including what each one does best, what it costs, and where it may fall short for your needs.


## Topline Pro


Topline Pro handles the same office work as Housecall Pro. It also does all your marketing and lead gen work for you, so you can focus on serving your clients.


While Housecall Pro can build an SEO-optimized website, it leaves the tedious work of staying visible and up to date on your shoulders. Topline Pro, on the other hand, writes and publishes ongoing SEO-focused blog posts, Google Business Profile updates, and social media posts for you every month.


Want to know where your website is helping (or hurting) your ability to get found? **** Run it through Topline Pro’s free[site health checker.](https://app.toplinepro.com/online-health-report)


The software automatically reaches out to satisfied customers to ask them for Google reviews, so you can build your social proof without lifting a finger. Upload a few photos from the jobs you're most proud of. Topline Pro then transforms them into Showcase pages that beautifully display your craftsmanship and garner you new leads.


“Within one hour of the new site and SEO going live, I got my first booking for a gutter cleaning and window cleaning job,” claimed one[reviewer](https://www.toplinepro.com/toplinepro-reviews) .


Of course, the core tools you’d expect after a lead comes in, like quotes, scheduling, customer management, invoices, and payments, are also part of the package.


Topline Pro’s basic pricing starts higher than Housecall Pro’s lowest tier, but you’re getting more bang for your buck. That’s because Topline Pro stands in as your company’s automated marketer, saving you time and money you’d otherwise spend on your website, SEO, social media, reviews, and finding new work.


**Best for:** Small home-service businesses that want their website, SEO, social media, reviews, and lead generation handled automatically alongside quoting, scheduling, invoicing, and payments.


**Drawbacks:** Topline Pro starts at a higher price than Housecall Pro’s entry-level plans, so it may not make sense if you only need basic scheduling, invoicing, and customer management.


**Pricing (annual):**


- ‍ **Starter Plan** $159/month **‍**
- **Core Plan** $199/month **‍**
- **Pro Plan** $239/month


## Jobber


Jobber is ideal for organizations that need more flexible and powerful route planning than Housecall Pro.


Housecall Pro’s route optimization tool is only available on more expensive plans. And even then, it only lets your dispatchers rearrange jobs for one technician within a single day, rather than optimizing several people and days together.


Jobber's plans start at $29/mo for a single user, but the routing and custom-field features that go head-to-head with Housecall Pro live on the Grow plan, which starts at $149/mo when billed annually.


All of Jobber’s plans let you optimize routes for one employee, a group, or your whole team, and plan as many as seven days at once.


Jobber also gives you considerably more freedom to customize the information you track. Custom fields can be added for clients, properties, quotes, jobs, invoices, and team members. Housecall Pro introduced more flexible custom fields in 2026, but they currently apply to jobs only, with customer-profile and estimate fields still planned for a later release.


**Best for:** Small home-service teams with lots of daily stops, or businesses that want more flexibility in how they track customer, property, and job data.


**Drawbacks:** Housecall Pro currently offers some marketing capabilities Jobber doesn’t match directly, and several of Jobber’s more useful operational features require higher plans. Route optimization starts on Connect, while richer quoting and job costing require Grow.


**Pricing (annual):**


- ‍ **Core** $29/month **‍**
- **Connect** $99/month **‍**
- **Grow** $149/month **‍**
- **Plus** custom pricing


## Workiz


If you run a call-heavy office or want better inventory tracking, Workiz is a step up from Housecall Pro.


With Genius Phone, admins can see active calls, listen in without interrupting, privately “whisper” advice to the employee on the call, or join the conversation themselves. Call Insights then automatically transcribes and summarizes calls, makes the transcript searchable, and pulls out details such as the job type, address, and pricing discussed. These features, which are more than you get with Housecall Pro’s equivalent “CSR AI” software, are useful for an owner managing several dispatchers or CSRs who wants to know how calls are being handled without listening to every recording from beginning to end.


Workiz also has an edge if your crews carry a lot of parts. Housecall Pro can track materials used on jobs and now supports purchase orders in some trade-specific packages. But its own inventory guidance still points businesses toward QuickBooks Online Plus for true inventory tracking.


Workiz’s Ultimate plan gives you an inventory system that tracks the quantity, cost, and sale value of stock by location. “Locations” can include warehouses, offices, or individual vehicles, and Workiz keeps a record of changes when you move stock between them.


**Best for:** Call-heavy service businesses that want better visibility into how office staff handles customer calls, or teams that need to track inventory.


**Drawbacks:** Some[users mention](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.workiz&utm_source=chatgpt.com#:~:text=This%20app%20is%20an,Now%20both%20versions%20suck.) that the mobile app, particularly the Android version, can be laggy and glitchy.


**Pricing:** Prospective buyers will have to reach out to sales for pricing.


## ServiceTitan


ServiceTitan is the heavyweight option on this list. It handles the same field-service basics as Housecall Pro, but adds layers of operational control that help as a company adds technicians, managers, locations, and more complicated jobs.


Dispatching is a good example. ServiceTitan’s Dispatch Pro doesn’t just look for the closest technician. It can weigh technician skills, recent performance, location, drive time, and the predicted value of a job when recommending who should get the call. You can also tell it whether to prioritize shorter drives, higher average tickets, or a mix of both.


ServiceTitan also gives larger companies more tools for managing performance across the business. Its Field Pro product records technician-customer conversations, provides technicians with pre-job briefs and AI-guided equipment diagnostics, and lets managers score calls and identify coaching opportunities afterward. That may not be useful when you only have two techs you talk to every day, but it’s valuable when you have a field team large enough that managers can’t ride along with everyone.


**Best for:** Larger, more complex home-service businesses that need sophisticated dispatching, technician performance management, commercial workflows, or centralized control across multiple locations.


**Drawbacks:** ServiceTitan’s depth comes with substantially more complexity. As one[reviewer](https://www.reddit.com/r/HVAC/comments/1c4g3pi/whats_your_biggest_problem_with_service_titan/) put it, “ServiceTitan can do everything, but it’s like giving a Ferrari to someone who just needs a pickup truck.”


Reviews frequently call out difficult onboarding and a steep learning curve, and its mobile app has attracted complaints about reliability and cumbersome workflows. It also makes less sense for a small team that doesn’t have office staff or managers to take advantage of its deeper reporting, dispatching, and coaching tools.


**Pricing:** Prospective buyers will have to reach out to sales for pricing.


## QuoteIQ


QuoteIQ is a mobile-first Housecall Pro alternative designed for home service businesses that rely on square footage for accurate estimates.


All you have to do is enter a property address, and QuoteIQ’s MapMeasure Pro tool pulls up satellite imagery, where you can measure roofs, lawns, driveways, concrete, fences, and other areas without making a separate site visit. Its AI Measurement tool can automatically trace surfaces, while AI Pitch Detection factors roof slope into the square-footage calculation. Once you have the measurements, you can apply your own pricing to build the estimate.


Note that MapMeasure Pro and QuoteIQ Cam aren't included on QuoteIQ's entry-level Essentials plan; you'll need the Beginner tier or higher to get them.


You can also use QuoteIQ Cam to capture 4K job photos and video, inspection forms, annotations, before-and-after images, and cloud storage tied to the customer and job. That feature is less of a differentiator from Housecall Pro than it once was, though: Housecall Pro now has photo annotations, timestamps, custom checklists, videos, and job galleries as well.


Like Housecall Pro, you can speak directly to QuoteIQ’s AI Autopilot. The system can execute tasks across 35 tools, including creating estimates, sending invoices, rescheduling jobs, texting customers, tracking expenses, and pulling business data.


**Best for:** Contractors who quote measurement-heavy work from their phone, especially roofing, landscaping, lawn care, concrete, and exterior-service businesses.


**Drawbacks:** QuoteIQ is a younger platform, and some[Google Play reviewers](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=corp.quoteiq.app&hl=en_US) have reported bugs and reliability problems.


**Pricing (annual):**


- ‍ **Essentials** $25/month **‍**
- **Beginner** $62.50/month **‍**
- **Pro** $125/month **‍**
- **Elite** $249.17/month **‍**
- **Max** $582.50/month


## Townsquare Interactive


Townsquare Interactive isn’t a full-fledged field service management tool like Housecall Pro. You'd still need a separate tool for back-office administrative tasks.


Instead, it focuses almost exclusively on building and managing small business websites and social media accounts.


Housecall Pro uses AI to build your website and optimize it for search before they turn it back over to you to fill with content. Townsquare’s team, on the other hand, does all the blog and social media posting to keep your customer-facing marketing fresh and updated.


There is a lightweight business-management platform underneath that marketing service, including a CRM, an inbox, a calendar, online booking, estimates, invoices, payments, and automated email and SMS. But Townsquare isn’t centered on technician dispatching, route optimization, time tracking, pricebooks, job costing, or other tools for managing crews in the field.


**Best for:** Small home-service businesses that want a managed website and ongoing local SEO rather than another DIY marketing toolkit.


**Drawbacks:** With a managed service, you’re depending much more heavily on the provider to execute well.


Some reviewers have complained about slow website launches, poor communication, SEO results that didn’t meet expectations, and difficulty canceling.


One[Google reviewer](https://reviews.birdeye.com/townsquare-interactive-missoula-155662688693376) said the company was “non-responsive” and didn’t meet the website timeline they were promised.


**Pricing:** Prospective buyers will have to reach out to sales for pricing.


## FieldPulse


FieldPulse believes it should adapt to the way you work. Its ClearPath tool lets you build custom step-by-step checklists for your most common installation and maintenance jobs.


Within each stage, you can require specific actions, give different instructions to technicians and office staff, and trigger actions such as customer notifications. The mobile view shows technicians the steps and information relevant to the stage they’re working on.


FieldPulse has a clear advantage over Housecall Pro in inventory management. You can track stock separately across trucks, warehouses, and other locations, transfer parts between them, set minimum stock levels, scan barcodes in the field, and automatically create purchase orders when inventory falls below a set threshold. Housecall Pro still recommends its users rely on QuickBooks Online Plus, or its Ply integration, for full inventory tracking.


On the marketing side of the house, FieldPulse partners with Marketing 360, a third-party platform, to build search-optimized websites, run local service Google ads, create social posts, and monitor customer reviews.


If you like FieldPulse’s deeper workflow and inventory tools but also want outside help generating demand, the Marketing 360 integration gives you a way to combine the two.


**Best for:** Growing service businesses that want highly customizable field workflows, stronger inventory management, and the option to connect their FSM data to managed marketing services.


**Drawbacks:** FieldPulse’s flexibility can mean more setup than a smaller business needs, and some of its broader capabilities depend on add-ons or partner products rather than the core platform.


Recent[Google Play reviews](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.fieldpulse.app&utm_source=chatgpt.com) have also raised concerns about the mobile experience, including job photos failing to upload and cumbersome workflows for notes and estimates.


**Pricing:** Prospective buyers will have to reach out to sales for pricing.


## Service Fusion


If your business is growing fast and you want to keep software costs in check, take a look at Service Fusion.


The starting price is higher than Housecall Pro’s, so it’s not especially attractive for a solo operator, but every plan includes unlimited users. That makes it a much more interesting option once you have several technicians, dispatchers, or office staff who all need access.


It’s also a solid option for businesses that do a lot of jobs where cell service and WiFi are limited. Housecall Pro doesn’t offer much in the way of offline capability: Its[help center](https://help.housecallpro.com/en/articles/4747652-housecall-pro-mobile-faq?utm_source=chatgpt.com) says jobs are the only area where data can be stored, and technicians must first open the job while they still have service.


Service Fusion’s new Offline Mode lets technicians take job notes, add photos and documents, and complete job tasks without a connection, then sync those changes automatically once service returns.


That difference could matter for plumbers working in basements, HVAC techs in mechanical rooms, or crews covering rural service areas.


**Best for:** Growing service businesses that want predictable software costs as they add technicians, dispatchers, and office staff, as well as businesses that need mobile capabilities in complex environments.


**Drawbacks:** Service Fusion is expensive for very small teams, and its mobile apps have[drawn repeated complaints](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.servicefusion.react) about speed and reliability.


[Independent comparisons](https://www.capterra.com/compare/135788-140363/Service-Fusion-vs-HouseCall-Pro) also score Housecall Pro higher for ease of use, functionality, value for money, and customer service.


**Pricing (annual):**


- ‍ **Starter** $208/month **‍**
- **Plus** $325/month **‍**
- **Pro** $533/month


## ServiceM8


ServiceM8 has built most of its features around Apple devices, so it’s a good option for teams that rely heavily on their iPhones and iPads. Its iOS app supports things like Siri shortcuts, voice-tagged job photos, document scanning, AR measurements, Apple Watch notifications, and 3D room scans.


Field staff can view job information and schedules, take photos and videos, collect signatures, and update jobs without an internet connection. Notes and photos saved offline sync back to the account once the device reconnects.


ServiceM8’s paid plans include unlimited users and scale mainly by the number of new jobs created each month.


**Best for:** Small, iPhone- or iPad-based service teams that want to run jobs from the field and keep working when cell service drops.


**Drawbacks:** ServiceM8 is still an Apple-first product.


It now offers ServiceM8 Lite for Android, but ServiceM8 itself says the iPhone and iPad app is the[better, fully featured experience](https://support.servicem8.com/help-center/tips-trick-more/more/does-servicem8-support-android-based-devices-yes) and says Android is intended for core field workflows only.


An August 2026[Google Play reviewer](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?hl=en&id=com.servicem8.skip) described the Android version as “completely watered down” compared with iOS and complained about slow syncing and jobs not appearing properly.


**Pricing (monthly):** Plans start at $29/mo, though a free tier for a single user is available.
